minutes.headline: Assessors approved April 22 and May 6 minutes, heard status reports, and entered executive session on abatement applications.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's status report on abatements, omitted bills and settled ATB cases, approved two sets of prior minutes, and got updates on the neighborhood review team and the website rollout. Deferral liens, exemption notices and a letter on misstated exemptions came up in board comment. The board then moved into executive session on abatement applications under c.59 s.60, and the recording ends there.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; no one was on Zoom and no one from the public spoke.

votes.motion: Accept the April 22nd minutes (seconded; only two members could vote, noted as approved)
Approve the May 6th minutes as amended (so moved and seconded; the two voting members voted together)
Enter executive session under purpose 7 (c.59 s.60) to review abatement applications, not to return to open session

budget_items.what_was_said: The abatement period closed with a count of abatements, including personal property and lake-area ones; inspections are more than half done.
Another omitted bill for a missed building goes out May 28; four ATB cases from FY2023 were settled.
A reimbursement form for motor vehicle excise on veterans exemptions was submitted to the Department of Revenue on May 1.
One new invoice for the ATB case settlement was reviewed and signed by the board.
A member said deferred taxes carry automatic interest and any change would need a town vote.

decisions.decision: Neighborhood review subcommittee tentatively plans its first meeting in the second week of June, then July, aiming to finish by end of August.
Assessing calendar discussion postponed to June 3.
Next meeting June 3 definite; June 10 room to be reserved for abatement follow-up; July scheduling to be revisited June 3.
A member volunteered to draft a policy format for the board.
Board to review the website again in about two weeks after the webmaster meeting Thursday.
A member will take the draft letter on misstated exemptions to the town manager to revise.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main items: the $450 MLS settlement bill, the omitted bill mailed May 28, the MD1 reimbursement and the four FY2023 ATB settlements. They differ in how much each records: ours has the scheduling and policy decisions and the 8% deferral interest, and the official minutes have the Circuit Breaker bill deferral and Sarah Cammer's swearing-in status. A reader should know the "$150 per" in ours could not be matched to the official minutes and needs checking against the recording.
